1: use ruff_diagnostics::{Diagnostic, Edit, Fix, FixAvailability, Violation};
2: use ruff_macros::{derive_message_formats, ViolationMetadata};
3: use ruff_python_ast::{self as ast, Expr};
4: use ruff_python_trivia::{SimpleTokenKind, SimpleTokenizer};
5: use ruff_text_size::{Ranged, TextSize};
6: 
7: use crate::checkers::ast::Checker;
8: use crate::Locator;
9: 
10: /// ## What it does
11: /// Checks for unnecessary dictionary unpacking operators (`**`).
12: ///
13: /// ## Why is this bad?
14: /// Unpacking a dictionary into another dictionary is redundant. The unpacking
15: /// operator can be removed, making the code more readable.
16: ///
17: /// ## Example
18: /// ```python
19: /// foo = {"A": 1, "B": 2}
20: /// bar = {**foo, **{"C": 3}}
21: /// ```
22: ///
23: /// Use instead:
24: /// ```python
25: /// foo = {"A": 1, "B": 2}
26: /// bar = {**foo, "C": 3}
27: /// ```
28: ///
29: /// ## References
30: /// - [Python documentation: Dictionary displays](https://docs.python.org/3/reference/expressions.html#dictionary-displays)
31: #[derive(ViolationMetadata)]
32: pub(crate) struct UnnecessarySpread;
33: 
34: impl Violation for UnnecessarySpread {
35:     const FIX_AVAILABILITY: FixAvailability = FixAvailability::Sometimes;
36: 
37:     #[derive_message_formats]
38:     fn message(&self) -> String {
39:         "Unnecessary spread `**`".to_string()
40:     }
41: 
42:     fn fix_title(&self) -> Option<String> {
43:         Some("Remove unnecessary dict".to_string())
44:     }
45: }
46: 
47: /// PIE800
48: pub(crate) fn unnecessary_spread(checker: &mut Checker, dict: &ast::ExprDict) {
49:     // The first "end" is the start of the dictionary, immediately following the open bracket.
50:     let mut prev_end = dict.start() + TextSize::from(1);
51:     for ast::DictItem { key, value } in dict {
52:         if key.is_none() {
53:             // We only care about when the key is None which indicates a spread `**`
54:             // inside a dict.
55:             if let Expr::Dict(inner) = value {
56:                 let mut diagnostic = Diagnostic::new(UnnecessarySpread, value.range());
57:                 if let Some(fix) = unnecessary_spread_fix(inner, prev_end, checker.locator()) {
58:                     diagnostic.set_fix(fix);
59:                 }
60:                 checker.diagnostics.push(diagnostic);
61:             }
62:         }
63:         prev_end = value.end();
64:     }
65: }
66: 
67: /// Generate a [`Fix`] to remove an unnecessary dictionary spread.
68: fn unnecessary_spread_fix(
69:     dict: &ast::ExprDict,
70:     prev_end: TextSize,
71:     locator: &Locator,
72: ) -> Option<Fix> {
73:     let source = locator.contents();
74:     if source.is_empty() {
75:         return None;
76:     }
77: 
78:     let dict_text = locator.slice(dict);
79:     let dict_lines = locator.lines_str(dict.range());
80:     if dict_text.is_empty() || dict_lines.is_empty() {
81:         return None;
82:     }
83: 
84:     let source_len = locator.text_len();
85:     let search_from = if prev_end > source_len {
86:         locator.floor_char_boundary(source_len)
87:     } else {
88:         locator.floor_char_boundary(prev_end)
89:     };
90: 
91:     let mut doublestar = None;
92:     for tok in SimpleTokenizer::starts_at(search_from, source) {
93:         let kind = tok.kind();
94:         if kind.is_trivia() {
95:             continue;
96:         }
97:         match kind {
98:             SimpleTokenKind::DoubleStar => {
99:                 doublestar = Some(tok);
100:                 break;
101:             }
102:             _ => {
103:                 if tok.start() > dict.end() {
104:                     break;
105:                 }
106:             }
107:         }
108:     }
109:     let doublestar = doublestar?;
110: 
111:     if let Some(last) = dict.iter_values().last() {
112:         let last_end = last.end();
113:         let mut edits = Vec::new();
114:         for tok in SimpleTokenizer::starts_at(last_end, source) {
115:             let kind = tok.kind();
116:             if kind.is_trivia() {
117:                 continue;
118:             }
119:             match kind {
120:                 SimpleTokenKind::Comma => {
121:                     let comma_range = tok.range();
122:                     edits.push(Edit::range_deletion(comma_range));
123:                 }
124:                 SimpleTokenKind::RBrace => {
125:                     let brace_range = tok.range();
126:                     edits.push(Edit::range_deletion(brace_range));
127:                     break;
128:                 }
129:                 _ => {}
130:             }
131:         }
132:         let leading_start = doublestar.start();
133:         let open_brace = dict.start() + TextSize::from(1);
134:         let leading_edit = Edit::deletion(leading_start, open_brace);
135:         Some(Fix::safe_edits(leading_edit, edits))
136:     } else {
137:         let deletion_start = doublestar.start();
138:         let deletion_end = dict.end();
139:         let deletion = Edit::deletion(deletion_start, deletion_end);
140:         Some(Fix::safe_edit(deletion))
141:     }
142: }

(End of file - total 142 lines)
